instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: After school, Coto went to Bolin’s house to begin investigating. Bolin pointed to an empty spot on a shelf and said, “This is where the stone normally is. You can see it’s not too big: about the size of a walnut.” Coto looked under, around, and further into the shelf. No real clues yet. Then, he heard a soft “meeeeow” come from behind him.

atoms.text:
“You have a cat!” exclaimed Coto.
“We do. Most people do because of the mice. Her name is Chi,” explained Bolin.
Coto asked, “Is she playful? Or does she climb where she shouldn’t?”
Bolin laughed, “Coto, it is clear you don’t have cats! Of course she does!”
Coto smiled, “Then she could have climbed up here and knocked the jade to the ground.”
Bolin immediately nodded his head. “That’s right! She could have. But if that’s true, then it should still be here, but it isn’t.”

atoms.text:
“Hmmm, let me think,” answered Coto. “Bolin, you think, too!”
Bolin laughed, “I already was thinking!” Just then, they saw Mai. She had been with her grandmother in the other room and was now crawling towards the sound of their laughs.
Bolin looked at Coto with excitement, “Coto, it was Mai! The cat knocked it off the shelf, and then Mai found it on the ground! She must have thought it was pretty and brought it to her room!”

atoms.text:
The two boys went into Mai’s room and searched through her toys. Many minutes later, Bolin, standing over Mai’s cot, yelled, “I’ve got it! I’ve got it! It was here under her mattress!” They ran to see Bolin’s grandmother and proudly showed her the family heirloom.
“My boys! How wonderful! I will prepare a feast in your honor to celebrate this wonderful find. You have given me back a piece of my family. Thank you so very much.” That evening, Coto ate the most magical food he had ever had and felt proud to have been able to help his friend.
